articleSummary: Taipei plastic surgeons warn that cross-border cosmetic procedures pose serious post-operative risks for patients returning from China or Korea. Post-operative care is the main challenge: brief overseas stays hinder ongoing monitoring, leaving Taiwanese physicians without complete medical records and raising repair difficulty. Materials used overseas differ from Taiwan regulations; some Chinese clinics reportedly use unnamed 'Ukrainian gel' for breast and buttock augmentation, which may migrate; Korea’s exosome and stem cell therapies can produce facial irregularities requiring home-based treatment. Documented cases include nasal ala necrosis from vascular embolism after hyaluronic acid in Korea, leg infections after overseas fillers, and an umbilical deformity after abdominal lift in China. Travel after surgery also increases infection, thrombosis, and slower recovery; thorough pre-op evaluation and long-term post-care plans are essential.

articleHeadline: Papaya juice not a cure: Dengue prompts rise in papaya leaf juice use; doctor cautions against delaying medical care
articleSummary: Rising dengue in India; by end of February, ~6,930 cases and 10 deaths; transmission earlier and longer; Delhi sees ongoing cases; Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka drive burden. Papaya leaf juice is widely used as folk remedy; however, evidence is weak: systematic review found only small, inconsistent studies showing modest platelet increase; no data on bleeding, plasma leakage, or survival; preparations are unregulated with variable active compounds; possible adverse effects include nausea, abdominal discomfort, allergic reactions, liver enzyme derangements with heavy use. Dengue management varies by patient; doctors consider platelet trends and overall condition, might require more tests or admission. Common mistakes include NSAIDs like ibuprofen or aspirin; should be avoided unless a clinician clears them. Early diagnosis, fluids, rest, and supervision remain essential; home remedies offer no proven benefit.

articleSummary: Angiostrongylus cantonensis (rat lungworm) was first described in 1933 in Guangzhou by H.T. Chen. The parasite cycles through rats, slugs and snails; humans ingest larvae via contaminated produce (notably lettuce) or undercooked intermediate hosts (freshwater prawns, frogs, crayfish, crabs, and some freshwater fish). In humans, larvae can reach the central nervous system, causing symptoms from headache, fever, fatigue, neck pain, numbness, and photophobia to meningitis, paralysis, coma, disability, or death. The parasite has spread beyond its origin to Southeast Asia, Australia, Latin America, and several U.S. areas, including Hawai'i, Florida, and the Gulf Coast. Roughly 7,000 global cases have been reported, about 10 per year in the U.S., mostly in Hawai'i. Diagnosis involves blood tests and meningitis evaluation; prevention emphasizes washing produce, cooking seafood and freshwater hosts to 165°F, and limiting snail/slug exposure in homes and with pets.

articleHeadline: How drug-resistant TB evades detection in standard tests
articleSummary: Rifampicin-resistant TB is not reliably detected by standard tests that screen only the 81-base-pair RRDR of rpoB. Resistance can arise from changes to rifampicin binding or from co-occurring mutations that boost bacterial fitness. Moving beyond RRDR, whole-genome sequencing (WGS) and targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) detect broader resistance; Deeplex Myc-TB has identified V170F and I491F mutations in sputum and stool. In rural labs, MAS-PCR and HRMA offer faster, cheaper alternatives, while nanopore sequencing promises portable, real-time detection. For high-burden countries like India, adopting non-RRDR diagnostics is essential to halt silent spread.

articleSummary: Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo strain in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Ituri, North Kivu, Bunia, Kinshasa) accelerates beyond the response. As of Aug 8, 2026, 4,141 confirmed cases and 1,889 deaths. Second-largest Ebola outbreak on record and the largest in DRC history, surpassing the 2018–2020 Kivu total (3,317) by late July; about 75 new cases and 35 deaths daily. Contact tracing has collapsed: roughly 10 contacts per case versus over 40 in Uganda’s, and 57 in Kivu; 90% of Bunia treatment-center admissions had no contact list; more than 70% of new cases and two-thirds of deaths arise from community transmission not under observation. North Kivu centers at 139% occupancy; Ituri at 57%. No licensed vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo; WHO reversed May guidance and approved Ervebo trial in DRC using ~500,000 doses held by Gavi. Frontline health-worker compensation negotiations ongoing with the government after August 5 statements; Uganda reported 20 imported cases, 15 from the DRC.
